dedupe_keys.name: tods transit operational data standard extending gtfs with runs deadheads and personnel

description: The Transit Operational Data Standard (TODS) is an open standard for describing how scheduled transit service is operated, so that runs, driver assignments and non-revenue movements can be moved between scheduling software, computer-aided dispatch and automatic vehicle location systems and between agencies. It was developed in 2021 and 2022 by a working group of agencies and vendors with resources from the California Integrated Travel Project (Cal-ITP), which also funded the TODS Board through 2025; the specification is hosted in MobilityData's GitHub. Coverage: generic standard, used by several software vendors and transit agencies, mainly in North America. TODS extends GTFS Schedule with files for deadheads (non-revenue trips and their stops), runs and run events, personnel assignments and supplemental changes, keeping GTFS identifiers so rider data and operational data stay linked; version 2.0 and later revisions are managed through a change process with a board and contributor licence agreement. Format and access: CSV-based specification with reference, examples and implementation guide on the TODS website and GitHub; free. Licence: Apache 2.0 for the repository content. Caveats: TODS datasets themselves are usually kept private to protect internal operations data, so the standard rarely comes with public data. Simulation uses: representing vehicle blocks, driver runs and deadheads in transit operations and capacity planning models, and in emergency response re-planning of bus service. Related records: the GTFS specification (data-gtfs-specification) is the base it extends, and the Cal-ITP transit data (data-cal-itp-california-transit-gtfs-analyses) come from the same state programme.
